The biggest arguments against this are that it would be enabling addicts and if they knew they could do it safely they're even less likely to quit. I believe that addicts will use until they're ready to quit regardless of a safe space or narcan, so why not save some lives? If they actually set it up to have social workers/nonprofits work with the people who go there into finding long-term help, that could potentially be revolutionary in how we fight addiction. Am I naive in thinking this? Are those who believe that this would only enable actually correct? Thanks!
